description:
I am Sean Alvin, a high-school student in Jakarta with roots in East Kalimantan.

For Field Shift I built TanahCerdas, a bilingual (English/Bahasa Indonesia) crop-rotation tool for rice farmers in Kutai Kartanegara. It replays 21 years of NASA POWER and GPM IMERG data through an FAO-56 water balance to compare second-season crops on profit, soil health and drought risk. It also connects to my own research: a lab-calibrated, temperature-compensated capacitive soil (HW-390) moisture sensor.
